correctness.rationale: Necessary σ(n)>=2n rules out ≤4 distinct odd primes because the maximal abundance at 3,5,7,11 is 2304/1155<2. For 5 prime factors, monotone abundance forces 3,5,7,s,t with s in {11,13,17,19}; σ=192(s+1)(t+1), so t<=floor[192(s+1)/(18s-192)], namely 384,64,30,25. Exactly 71+12+3+1=87 prime t cases. Since n=105st is squarefree, its 16 complementary pairs correspond to divisors d|105s, with weights d+(105s/d)t. A complement-closed selection sums to 2n iff these weights have a subset sum 2n. Independently re-enumerated all 87 and rejected exact subset sums using a fresh meet-in-middle implementation over directly enumerated complementary divisors; this exhausts all 5-prime candidates *because of the unbounded abundance reduction*, not an arbitrary cutoff. For n=937365 direct products and omitted pair sum 60630, σ=1935360, yield retained sum 2n. The six-prime witness is explicitly prior.
